The Battle of Polom Barracks (Croatian: Vojarna Polom), part of the Yugoslav People's Army (JNA), was a military operation carried out in the town of Doljani (Daruvar, Croatia) between 16 and 17 September 1991. It consisted of a Croatian offensive aimed at capturing the barracks and obtaining the military equipment stored there. The clash occurred within the broader context of the Croatian War of Independence, which escalated openly in August 1991, and as part of the Battle of the Barracks in September of that year.
The operation was successful for the Croatian forces, who were able to seize a significant amount of military material, which was later used to organize brigades that would fight in Western Slavonia.
Polom Barracks
The Polom Barracks were located west of the Daruvar–Pakrac route, about 5 km south of Daruvar, in the village of Doljani, with around 1,003 inhabitants. The area was hilly and surrounded by dense forests, making it difficult to observe from the road, which was about 20 meters above the barracks. There were two entrances: one to the north sector where the barracks were located (45°33'36.43"N 17°12'38.58"E) and one to the south, mainly for depots and ammunition storage (45°33'13.82"N 17°12'7.71"E). Both were internally connected by a road.
The garrison depended on the XXXII Corps of the JNA, whose command post and most units were in Varaždin, under siege since 11 September 1991 (captured by Croatian forces on the 22nd). Under this Corps was the Bjelovar Garrison, also under siege since 14 September (captured on the 29th). Bjelovar was the base of the 265th Mechanized Brigade of the JNA, classified as A, the command of the 28th Partisan Division (to be mobilized) and one of its partisan brigades, the First (also to be mobilized).
The 28th Division, under Colonel Nikola Marić, had the 21st "Jan Žižka" Brigade stationed in Doljani. By the time of the battles, this small garrison had been significantly reduced due to early desertions. Only about 20 Serbian and Albanian members remained.
